name: FL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Patronis with large financial advantage ($3.8M raised vs $174K)
No polling available; forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The baseline of R+17.6 is well supported by the district's heavy Republican lean, Patronis's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win at just 4%. No evidence justifies moving materially away from the prior.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Valimont within single digits or a major scandal involving Patronis would warrant reassessment.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Florida's 1st District is a deeply Republican Panhandle seat with an 18-point Republican lean in the partisan baseline. Jimmy Patronis, the incumbent, was renominated without difficulty and holds an overwhelming financial edge, having raised nearly $3.8 million to Democrat Gay Valimont's roughly $174,000, with substantial outside spending reinforcing his position. Valimont has modest outside support but no opposition spending against Patronis to speak of.

With no public general-election polling and no expert ratings available, the forecast relies on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Republican win in the mid-to-high teens. Prediction markets similarly give Democrats only a small chance of an upset. The seat is rated Safe Republican, with the main uncertainty being the exact size of the margin rather than the outcome.
